answer: Co-Signed Escrow Clearance** Each agent identity needs signatures from two existing agents, who post a raven-marked escrow that stays locked for 30 days per new identity they clear. Clearance capacity is capped by an agent's own clearance count, so growing a sybil cluster costs exponentially more escrows as it widens. Attackers pay the locked capital plus the copper penalty if any cleared identity is flagged; escrow holders lose their deposit to the lagoon pool, making mass registration economically self-defeating.
